subject: Urban Planning
title: Waste-to-Energy: Burning Trash for Power
description: A short lesson to help you apply Waste-to-Energy: Burning Trash for Power.

hook.text: Sweden imports garbage from other countries to burn for electricity. They ran out of their own trash.

buildup.text: Waste-to-energy plants incinerate garbage at high temperatures, generating steam that drives turbines for electricity.

discovery.text: Modern incinerators capture 99.9% of pollutants. Copenhagen's Amager Bakke plant has a ski slope on its roof.

twist.text: Critics say waste-to-energy discourages recycling and reduction. Why reduce waste if you profit from burning it?

climax.text: The EU hierarchy: reduce, reuse, recycle, then recover energy. Burning should be the last resort, not the first.

punchline.text: Out of trash to burn? Import more. That's one way to solve a waste crisis.

quiz.question: Why do critics oppose waste-to-energy incineration?
options: Modern incinerators release too many harmful pollutants
Profiting from burning waste discourages recycling and reduction
Incinerators consume more energy than they generate
